subject: PSHE
framework: Statutory guidance: Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education (revised, in force from 1 September 2026); National Curriculum in England: Citizenship programmes of study KS3 and KS4; PSHE Association programme of study (non-statutory reference); EYFS PSED for Reception. School position: PSHE only in every year group, with no RSE or sex education; puberty and bulugh taught from Year 7 to boys and girls separately
statusNote: Provisional. Read in full text from official sources: the 1 September 2026 RSHE statutory guidance PDF, compared line by line with the July 2025 PDF (the two extracts are identical; the 2026 file is the July 2025 text reissued); National Curriculum citizenship KS3 and KS4 (official PDF); the EYFS PSED goals (framework from 1 September 2026); the gov.uk collection page. The DfE will not publish standalone gender-questioning guidance: it proposes to put that content in Keeping children safe in education (policy paper, 12 February 2026), so nothing separate exists to read. Not verified: the PSHE Association programme of study download (learning opportunities by key stage), which could not be opened in October 2026; its core themes (Health and wellbeing, Relationships, Living in the wider world) come from earlier reads of site pages. Year allocation is a recommended sequence. School decisions recorded (October 2026, updated 26 October): the subject is PSHE only in every year group, with no RSE or sex education (manners, friendships, families, health and hygiene, and keeping safe, including body safety at a non-sexual level and what the law says to protect young people); puberty and bulugh are taught from Year 7 to boys and girls separately; parents can see all PSHE materials. Statements below quote the national guidance; the school's lessons follow these decisions. Year 1 was rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack: one unit per half term, following Tarbiyyah Primary's Cornerstones projects (2026-27 order), White Rose maths and Little Wandle phonics. Years 2 to 9 were rebuilt in November 2026 to the TGA curriculum packs (docs/curriculum-packs/y2.md to y9.md): one unit per half term, titled by half term so the portal planner places each one. November 2026 alignment with the school's own files: Years 7 to 9 follow the order and topics of the Tarbiyyah Secondary PSHE Curriculum Intent (Year 7: transition, safeguarding, wellbeing, identity and protected characteristics, growing up, first aid basics; Year 8: first aid, British values and law, respect and risk, wellbeing, helping those less fortunate, families in Britain; Year 9: marriage, family and the law, careers and options, staying safe, a community project). The PSHE folder holds the PSHE Association KS3-4 Planning Toolkit (2017), a generic planning document; only content that fits the school's rules is used (no sexuality, romance, contraception, STIs, sexting or pornography lessons). November 2026 alignment: Years 1 to 6 follow Tarbiyyah Primary's PSHE scheme of work and PSHE long-term plan (the Ealing LA PSHE, Citizenship and SEAL spiral scheme, a local-authority scheme: Year A units in Years 1, 3, 5 and Year B units in Years 2, 4, 6), with every RSE and puberty lesson left out, theme weeks and festival dates not adopted, and fund-raising adapted to a sadaqah plan at home. Owner decision, 9 Nov 2026: the Year 8 and Year 9 relationships topics in the intent are taught as law and citizenship (British law, with the Islamic teaching on marriage alongside, respect for every person, no RSE content, no promotion); puberty and bulugh are taught in Year 7 only, boys and girls separately.

purpose: PSHE helps pupils stay safe and healthy and form respectful relationships, taught within an Islamic ethos.
Primary pupils (Years 1 to 6): adab, friendships, families, health, hygiene and keeping safe, including body safety. The subject is PSHE only.

Secondary pupils (Years 7 to 11): PSHE taught from an Islamic perspective, with puberty and bulugh taught in Year 7 to boys and girls separately: marriage and family, modesty, puberty and its fiqh, consent and the law, online harms and mental wellbeing.
Citizenship prepares pupils to take an active part in society, including democracy, law, rights and personal finance.

statements: Self-regulation: understand feelings and begin to manage behaviour
Managing self: show independence, perseverance and understanding of rules
Building relationships: play co-operatively, take turns and show sensitivity to others
Families: different family types should be respected; know how to seek help if home is unhappy or unsafe
Caring friendships: kind friendships include others and conflict is not handled with violence
Respectful relationships: respect others' boundaries and recognise bullying, including online
Online relationships: respect applies online; take care with personal information and strangers
Being safe: each body belongs to its owner; know how to report abuse and keep asking for help
Mental wellbeing: name emotions, know who to talk to and that mental health problems are common
Wellbeing online: balanced internet use, age restrictions, gaming risks and rights over personal data
Physical health, healthy eating and sleep support wellbeing
Drugs, alcohol, tobacco and vaping: learn facts and risks, including nicotine addiction
Basic first aid, including how to call emergency services
Developing bodies: the guidance lists puberty in upper primary; TGA teaches hygiene and modesty only, and puberty from Year 7

strands.strand: TGA position: PSHE only in primary
statements: Years 1 to 6 study PSHE only, with no sex education
Body safety (private parts are private, say no, go and tell) is taught as safeguarding
Puberty and its fiqh are taught from Year 7, to boys and girls separately
Families and committed relationships; forced marriage and marriage under 18 are illegal
Respectful relationships: consent, trust, tolerance, bystander duties and challenging stereotypes and misogyny
Online and media: fake accounts, AI-generated content, deepfakes, sharing images and the law, scams and sextortion
Being safe: consent and boundaries, harassment, domestic abuse, coercive control, grooming and exploitation, FGM and forced marriage
Islam places intimacy only within marriage; pupils learn the law on consent and basic sexual health facts in Year 11
Puberty and bulugh: changes, ghusl and new duties, taught in Year 7 to boys and girls separately
Mental wellbeing and wellbeing online: managing anxiety, gambling harms, misinformation and curated images
Drugs, alcohol, tobacco and vaping: illegal and illicit vapes, drug supply law, alcohol risks and dependency
Health protection and the healthcare system: vaccines, sleep, screening, NHS services and medical consent
Physical health, healthy eating and personal safety, including knife crime and exploitation signs
Basic first aid: treating common injuries, CPR and the purpose and use of defibrillators
Suicide prevention and eating disorders may be taught, after consulting mental health professionals and training staff

strands.strand: Faith and withdrawal (as stated in the guidance)
statements: Schools with a religious character may teach their faith perspective and must make clear when content reflects belief
Parents may request withdrawal from some or all sex education; the head must discuss it and document the process
Primary heads must grant a withdrawal request; secondary heads may refuse only in exceptional circumstances
From three terms before a pupil turns 16 they may opt back in, and the school must make pupils aware
Parents cannot withdraw from relationships or health education, or from science including puberty and reproduction
Pupils learn the facts and law on biological sex and gender reassignment; contested views are not taught as fact
TGA: puberty and bulugh are taught to boys and girls separately, and parents can see all PSHE materials

toKS4: Years 10 and 11 continue PSHE (taught from an Islamic perspective; puberty and bulugh are taught in Year 7 only, boys and girls separately) and add National Curriculum KS4 citizenship content (law, rights, democracy and personal finance). School content for Years 10 and 11 already covers stress, relationships and the law, gambling and exploitation, work, post-16 pathways, money, first aid, and consent, modesty and the law. There is no examination in this programme and no board unit references. Key stage 3 builds the vocabulary, safe-help habits and legal awareness these units extend.

links.how: Science teaches human reproduction factually from Year 7 (KS2 science covers plant and animal life cycles only); PSHE gives the Islamic framing, choices and safety
Computing teaches how systems work; PSHE covers safe, respectful behaviour and reporting

Percentages, interest and calculations support budgeting, borrowing and payslip work
Money, work and consumer topics connect to business finance and employment law
History explains how democracy and rights developed; Citizenship covers how they operate now
Speaking, listening and critical reading support discussion of online content and body image
Pupils meet the same virtues in Islamic Studies and in character education
